a84.speaker: Thomas Kazungu Karisa, Kenyan farmer and cash-transfer recipient
a84.speech: "My family often went to bed hungry, my children were sent home from school for unpaid fees and I was buried in debt," said Karisa, a father of five. "If they had given me food, it would have been long gone by now," Karisa told AFP. "But with the money, I have been able to change my life."

a84.speaker: GiveDirectly (organization)
a84.speech: Believes charities and NGOs should stop handing out things like food and school books, and start just sending people cash. Said fears the money would be misused or wasted were unfounded, citing a Kenyan study that found families generated $2.50 for every $1 received, and says 80 percent of donations goes directly into the hands of recipients.

a84.speaker: Caroline Teti, GiveDirectly's Vice President for Risk in Africa
a84.speech: "We can show evidence of cash having reversed domestic violence, improved child mortality, improved business outcomes, made families healthier, children accessing more education," said Caroline Teti. "Cash is not a magic bullet," Teti said, adding that governments are still needed for fundamentals like schools, health facilities and electricity. "Poverty doesn't wait," Teti said. "One year is enough for a girl to drop out of school… for a mother or child to die." ; "Lives can only be changed by the people who are living that life," Teti said. "We are giving them dignity and we are giving them choice."

a84.speaker: University of Washington (2022 study)
a84.speech: Found that back-office costs in the United States ate up 30 to 60 percent of budgets for global health projects.

a84.speaker: Tariq Riebl, Norwegian Refugee Council Strategy and Innovation Director
a84.speech: Said the Norwegian Refugee Council now gives 20 percent of its aid in cash, but could easily give as much as 45 percent ; told AFP the only real obstacle is "latent conservatism" in the aid sector: "There's something more comforting about handing over a kit of non-food items or a sack of rice, than giving cash."

a84.speaker: USAID
a84.speech: Finally backed the use of cash payments in a policy paper last October, after years of internal pushback, before being gutted by the Trump administration.

a84.speaker: Tarak Bach Baouab, MSF Advocacy Head
a84.speech: "Cash for healthcare remains very rare," said Tarak Bach Baouab. "We want to be sure of the quality of our programmes so we prefer sourcing the drugs and equipment ourselves." ; "We're not there to tell people what to do with their lives. It's not very empowering and it creates a lot of dependency," Baouab said. "But if you give cash to a family and they don't spend it in the right way, then we might see health outcomes diminish."

a156.speaker: Salifou Lougué, CNSS Regional Director for the Boucle du Mouhoun
a156.speech: Said the Sourou valley was not a random choice; explained that it has been observed that this locality abounds with people carrying out self-employed activities without knowing how to provide for their old age, and that it is for this reason that the CNSS initiated this day to make them understand the importance of insuring themselves, to make the CNSS’s voluntary insurance known and to encourage their adherence to the product.

a156.speaker: Toussaint Bationo, Head of the CNSS Voluntary Insurance Promotion Service
a156.speech: Pointed out that, according to Article 22 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, everyone has the right to social security as a member of society; explained that the concept of social security is defined as a system of protection that society grants to its members through public measures against economic and social destitution and risks such as illness, disability, old age, unemployment, family burdens and death, hence the institution of the CNSS; said that in Burkina Faso the social security scheme applicable to salaried and similar workers is managed by the CNSS and governed by law n°015-2006/AN of 11 May 2006, and described the benefits provided by the CNSS and its sources of financing.

a156.speaker: Toussaint Bationo, Head of the CNSS Voluntary Insurance Promotion Service
a156.speech: Said it is not only civil servants who benefit from a retirement pension; indicated that the government instituted voluntary insurance by law N°015-2006/AN of 15 May 2006 (articles 4 and 5) and order n°2008-002/MTSS/SG/DGPS of 10 March 2008 in the hope of not leaving behind the actors of the liberal professions and the informal sector who work on their own account.

a156.speaker: Toussaint Bationo, Head of the CNSS Voluntary Insurance Promotion Service
a156.speech: In conclusion, indicated that social security is a right for every human being in general and for every Burkinabe in particular, and that it is the most elaborate form of solidarity, with the guarantee of the State; launched a strong appeal to all those who have an income to insure themselves in order to avoid disappointing tomorrows; at the end of the day did not hide his satisfaction at the turnout, the enthusiasm of the participants and the relevance of their questions.

a156.speaker: Issiaka Soro, president of the Union of Agricultural Cooperatives of the Sourou Valley (UCAVASO)
a156.speech: On behalf of the participants, congratulated the CNSS for this mission; according to him, the head of the Voluntary Insurance Promotion Service had not preached in the desert and convinced more than one person to subscribe to voluntary insurance; he also assured the mission that their exhortation would be relayed throughout the Sourou valley.

a177.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a177.speech: Spoke about the US government's support for the country, including the Global Fund, the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and the World Food Programme (WFP) ; recalled that part of this support remains suspended by decision of Donald Trump. However, he assured that he was working to ensure continued support in areas that are crucial to the country.

a177.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique (as source)
a177.speech: According to the Ministry of Finance, Vrooman recalled that part of this support remains suspended by decision of Donald Trump.

a177.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a177.speech: The American diplomat asked about the Government's new institutional structure.

a177.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Finance Minister
a177.speech: Commented that the current situation of suspension of financing creates imbalances in the proposal for the 2025 Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE).

a177.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Finance Minister
a177.speech: "Answering the question, the finance minister assured that it is focused on three main areas, the restructuring of the government machine; fiscal consolidation and good governance".

a177.speaker: Teresa Orjales, Spanish Ambassador to Mozambique
a177.speech: Demonstrated her country's openness to continue supporting Mozambique in its development policies and spoke about the 4th International Conference on Financing for Development that will take place in Seville, Spain, from June 30 to July 3, 2025: "This conference will be an opportunity to accelerate the implementation of the 2030 Agenda. It will also support the reform of the international financial architecture, it will also define the global financing agenda and advance the sustainable development goals".

a177.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Finance Minister
a177.speech: Welcomed the Spanish Government's willingness to continue supporting Mozambique and the invitation made for the country to participate in the Conference, as the country is a signatory to the 2030 Agenda and has participated in the reform of the international financial architecture.

a278.speaker: African Economic Outlook (AEO) report, African Development Bank
a278.speech: indicates that foreign direct investment (FDI) flows following the recent issuance of oil exploration licenses and the investment in infrastructure development is expected to spur Uganda's economy for most of 2018 ; indicates Uganda's economic performance generally remained strong despite the recent slowdown in real GDP growth, which is projected to reach 5.9% in 2018, up from 4.8% in 2017 and 2.3% in 2016; the increase in economic growth in 2018 is expected to be driven mainly by public infrastructure investment, recovery in manufacturing and construction, and improvements in the services sector; Uganda continues to have a low risk of debt distress, however the debt-to-GDP ratio is increasing and is projected to reach 45% by 2020.

a278.speaker: International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group debt sustainability analysis (2016)
a278.speech: gives Uganda's risk of debt distress a low rating.

a340.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin
a340.speech: Declared at the opening of the proceedings: "Decentralised governance must be the spearhead of public action, making it possible to satisfy basic needs and to launch our overall development."

a340.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin
a340.speech: Acknowledging past weaknesses and shortcomings, recalled that the reform was intended to break with the practices of the past, marked by confusion of roles, bad governance and impunity: "Should we have continued like that, or rather take courageous decisions to change things? We chose reform, and we must now make sure that it produces the expected results," he stressed ; insisted on the need for elected officials and technical staff to better internalise the spirit of the reform, which rests on a clear separation of functions: elected officials set the broad orientations, while the Executive Secretaries implement and manage in compliance with the rules of good governance.

a340.speaker: Luc Setondji Atrokpo, President of the National Association of Communes of Benin (ANCB)
a340.speech: On behalf of the communes, expressed his gratitude to the Head of State for the constant attention paid to local authorities: "No commune is left behind. Your actions are visible from North to South, from East to West and through the Centre," he affirmed with conviction, also welcoming the reform of the party system which, in his view, "stabilises communal councils and facilitates the implementation of the Communal Development Plans."

a340.speaker: Elected local officials (mayors and communal representatives)
a340.speech: Submitted a number of major concerns: the resumption of the issuance of customary landholding certificates (ADC), pending the generalisation of land titles, in order to secure land use and support communal finances; clarification of the status of mayors who are civil servants of the State, faced with complex administrative situations; and the integration of official vehicles into the communes' assets so that they can be reassigned in accordance with the texts.

a373.speaker: Marianne Young, British High Commissioner to Tanzania
a373.speech: Said her country will continue to provide development and humanitarian assistance as an important part of international cooperation; said they recognise that the United States has suspended the provision of aid until it carries out an assessment, but that the British government will maintain its firm commitment. “We believe that collaborative action among international partners is essential for advancing important development indicators, including the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).”

a373.speaker: Marianne Young, British High Commissioner to Tanzania
a373.speech: Said the donor community in Tanzania is closely following the changes in order to understand the possible effects; said Britain substantially increased the budget of the Overseas Development Institute (ODI) in the past year from 17 million pounds to more than 50 million pounds for 2024-2025. “Apart from that funding, we also use funds provided by the government through British International Investment, which has been a major stakeholder in Tanzania for more than 50 years. At present, our portfolio has 50 million pounds, and we aim to double this to 200 million pounds in the next few years. Also, we are considering using private funds. This is an important area in which the British government is fully cooperating with international institutions in order to increase financial support and address the existing funding shortfall.”

a373.speaker: Marianne Young, British High Commissioner to Tanzania
a373.speech: Said Britain ranks second in the size of foreign direct investment (FDI) in Tanzania and has major interests in various sectors including energy, infrastructure, and food and drink, and that British businesspeople regularly engage with the government over the challenges they encounter entering the Tanzanian market. “The main issues include transparency and predictability, especially regarding tax claims and investigations. We are pleased that the government accepted these problems and enabled discussions that led to the establishment of the Tax Commission, which has now begun its investigation. We look forward to the release of the Commission's report.” ; Asked whether they are satisfied with the time the government is taking, said the government quickly accepted their concerns and asked for specific examples, which they provided immediately along with evidence and corroborating data: “In response, the government quickly summoned the commissioners to investigate those matters. Now we are hopeful that recommendations will be submitted soon and that decisive action will follow immediately.”

a438.speaker: Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, Somali Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a438.speech: Called the successful repatriations a significant milestone in addressing the challenges of irregular migration and ensuring the safety of Somali nationals abroad ; "This operation highlights Somalia's unwavering commitment to its citizens and to addressing migration challenges through cooperation with our international partners," the minister said in a statement released on Thursday when the citizens returned from Libya.

a438.speaker: Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, Somali Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a438.speech: On Monday announced the successful repatriation of 22 Somali citizens who had been detained in Sudan's Dongola and Gadaref detention facilities for three months, saying all 22 arrived safely in Mogadishu, marking another milestone in the ministry's efforts to protect the rights and dignity of Somali citizens abroad and combat human trafficking.

a438.speaker: Somali Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a438.speech: Said the survivors of the early November boat tragedy, which claimed 28 lives in the Indian Ocean off Madagascar, shared harrowing accounts of their ordeal.

a438.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a438.speech: Said that every year, hundreds of Somali migrants embark on perilous journeys along the Northern Mediterranean route, passing through multiple countries with hopes of reaching Europe ; said insecurity, lack of food, shelter, and healthcare in Libya expose these migrants to significant risks, noting that thousands urgently require protection and humanitarian assistance.

a438.speaker: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix report published in July
a438.speech: Reported that more than 1,500 Somali migrants were stranded in Libya, where many face dangerous and precarious conditions.

a691.speaker: Michael C. Gonzales, U.S. Ambassador to Zambia
a691.speech: Recent revelation that US$20 million in American aid - intended for maize for drought relief in the nation - remained unaccounted for, and that the maize procured with these funds was bought at more than 48 percent above the market price.

a691.speaker: Michael C. Gonzales, U.S. Ambassador to Zambia
a691.speech: Claimed that Zambia loses US$3 billion to corruption annually.

a691.speaker: Michael C. Gonzales, U.S. Ambassador to Zambia
a691.speech: Addressing the media at the U.S Embassy in Lusaka recently, expressed disappointment over the UPND government's inability to prevent the diversion of essential medicines meant to be distributed free of charge to the Zambian public ; disclosed that since late 2021, U.S. investigations uncovered widespread theft of anti-retroviral, anti-malarial medications, and tuberculosis drugs supplied through American-funded programmes ; explained that according to the findings, 95 percent of pharmacies across the country were found selling these medicines, with 45 percent specifically distributing U.S donated supplies, adding that despite more than 13 months of repeated alerts and offers of technical support from the U.S, the situation remained unresolved ; clarified that the US$50 million was strictly part of the US$128 million funding each year for HIV, malaria, and TB interventions and not part of broader policy shifts in the United States ; stated that while medicines would continue to be delivered until January 2026 to avoid immediate stock-outs, no more shipments would follow unless the UPND government acted decisively.

a691.speaker: United States government
a691.speech: Announced a cut of US$50 million equivalent to K1.4 billion in annual aid to Zambia intended for medications and medical supplies, citing rampant theft of donor-funded drugs and the UPND government's failure to take decisive corrective action; announced earlier this month that it would cut the funding over the "systematic" theft of medicine and other supplies meant to be handed out for free to the most vulnerable but which had been found to be on sale in pharmacies.

a691.speaker: Ministry of Health of Zambia
a691.speech: Said it was taking action against the theft of donated medicines after the United States announced a major aid cut over the government's failure to tackle the racket ; said an independent forensic audit had also led to the removal from office of senior officials at the medical supplies agency, including its director general, and that other actions were expected.

a691.speaker: US Embassy in Zambia
a691.speech: Said the fraud was discovered in late 2021 but the UPND government had only arrested a few mid-level officials for involvement instead of tracking down the masterminds.

a691.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a691.speech: Campaigned on an anti-corruption platform, promising to clean up after the alleged excesses of former President Edgar Lungu; citizens were told corruption would be a thing of the past once he was voted into office.

a691.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a691.speech: Claims he has been able to rebrand Zambia to attract investments to avoid a return to the debilitating public debt that has been restructured by his administration since assuming office in 2021.

a691.speaker: President Hichilema's opponents
a691.speech: Charge that he has been divisive as a national leader, and that he has allowed graft to grow thereby exacerbating the dent in the UPND's selective anti-corruption fight.

a853.speaker: Washington (US government)
a853.speech: Threatened to press criminal charges, warning that "we will pursue criminal charges against those that engage in visa fraud and those who bring in and harbour illegal aliens", after it noted that "A nation without borders is not a nation".

a853.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a853.speech: Has not hidden his hostility to the BRICS mechanism, which he considers as opposed to the Washington liberal exclusionary order.

a853.speaker: The U.S. side
a853.speech: Issued strident denials of involvement after it was revealed that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was complicit in the extremist insurgent war in Nigeria.

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: Announced the launch of expanded commercial operations in Rwanda, marked by the transfer of the first delivery of responsibly sourced tantalum/niobium concentrate, also known as coltan, to its global trading partner.

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: Said that its partnership with a major international metals and minerals trading company provided it with a well-established global trading and marketing platform, and that the agreement allowed Aterian to access a network of downstream buyers and accelerate the development of its activities.

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: Explained on 15 September that, before commercial sales began, its partner had carried out extensive due diligence and testing to check product quality and compliance with a group of artisanal and small-scale mining suppliers in Rwanda that comply with OECD standards; following the success of this process, Eastinco, Aterian's wholly owned Rwandan subsidiary, activated its responsibly sourced tantalum and niobium supply chain and began trading.

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: Confirmed that a $250,000 mezzanine loan obtained to support its expansion had already been fully drawn and invested in trading operations, notably the acquisition of mineral concentrates from Rwanda.

a1047.speaker: Simon Rollason, CEO of Aterian
a1047.speech: "The successful completion of testing and supplier compliance checks, combined with the injection of new trading capital, now allows us to move forward at a sustained pace. We anticipate a significant increase in trading volumes over the coming weeks, thanks to the activation of multiple supply relationships and the strengthening of sourcing operations with our financial partners." ; "This is a pivotal moment for our trading business, which lays the commercial foundations for our growth in the region." ; "With our operations, our risk management systems and our partnerships now in place, we are confident in our ability to demonstrate full traceability compliance while building a robust supply chain with integrity, capable of supporting substantial volume growth and sustaining long-term revenue generation for the group."

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: Said that all of its mineral supplies came from the International Tin Supply Chain Initiative and were fully compliant with OECD due diligence guidelines, involving rigorous on-site audits, verification of mine of origin and conflict-free checks to guarantee the legitimacy and integrity of the supply chain; it also stressed that every supplier underwent a detailed onboarding and audit process covering operational, legal and ethical standards, and said these checks would continue and were essential to maintaining a regular supply of materials.

a1047.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
a1047.speech: According to the company, the partnership with its trading house validated its business model and opened a clear commercial path to establishing a vertically integrated exploration and trading platform for critical minerals across East Africa; Aterian confirmed that container-scale export sales were now ready to begin.

a1211.speaker: David Breux, IOM Chief of Mission in Côte d'Ivoire
a1211.speech: Said the post constitutes "a tool in the service of peace, mobility and cross-border cooperation."

a1211.speaker: Jessica Davis Ba, United States Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire
a1211.speech: Said this inauguration illustrates "solid cooperation between the American people and the Ivorian people." She stressed that security is the foundation of trade, investment and shared prosperity.

a1211.speaker: Vagondo Diomandé, Minister of the Interior and Security of Côte d'Ivoire
a1211.speech: Welcomed the constant support of international partners, recalling that this border post is both a symbol of national sovereignty and a lever for local and regional development.

a1412.speaker: Kalipso Chalkidou, World Health Organisation (WHO) Director for Health Financing and Economics
a1412.speech: Has warned that the world is facing a health financing emergency. Speaking at a regular press briefing for humanitarian agencies in Geneva, Switzerland, Chalkidou cautioned that as wealthier nations implement deep spending cuts, both international aid and national health systems are experiencing serious disruption. She cited recent decisions by the United States (US), several European governments and European Union bodies to freeze or reduce health aid.

a1412.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1412.speech: WHO forecasts suggest that global health investment is likely to fall by up to 40 percent this year, dropping by $10 billion from just over $25 billion in 2023. "The estimated $15 billion spent on health aid would bring the figure down to the lowest level in a decade," the health agency said. It added that the funding shortfall is creating a health financing emergency in many developing countries, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, which depend on external aid to fund their health systems. ; "In numerous countries, US-financed healthcare programmes were the primary source of external aid, accounting for as much as 30 percent of current health spending in countries like Malawi and around 25 percent in Mozambique and Zimbabwe," WHO said. ; The agency further raised concerns about rising debt burdens, saying many sub-Saharan African nations are grappling with soaring debt, with some spending twice as much on debt servicing as on health, making the reallocation of resources difficult.

a1412.speaker: WHO survey (cited by Kalipso Chalkidou)
a1412.speech: A WHO survey indicating that countries are now reporting health service disruptions "not seen since the peak of Covid-19".

a1412.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1412.speech: To address the crisis, WHO has urged countries to reduce aid dependency, increase revenue through improved taxation including health taxes on products like tobacco and alcohol, and collaborate with multilateral banks to secure low-interest loans for cost-effective health investments.

a1412.speaker: Government of Malawi
a1412.speech: The government insists it is doing everything possible to bridge the gap left by the aid cuts, although thousands of people employed through USAid-funded initiatives have already lost their jobs.

a1412.speaker: Malawian authorities
a1412.speech: Authorities have since called for a shift towards economic self-reliance, with an emphasis on entrepreneurship and partnerships with alternative international donors.

a1423.speaker: Mohammed Abdiker, IOM Chief of Staff
a1423.speech: "This partnership reflects a shared commitment to defending human dignity and justice. By directing faith-based donations toward global initiatives aimed at ending exploitation, we are responding to urgent needs, and we are setting out on the path to lasting change. Solidarity can translate into concrete action for those living in the shadow of conflict, poverty and displacement, and the Islamic Philanthropy Fund is a perfect example of this."

a1423.speaker: Irfan Rajput, Director of Programmes and Policy for Muslim Charity
a1423.speech: "More than 1,400 years ago, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) fought for the abolition of slavery and the preservation of human dignity. Inspired by these timeless values, Muslim Charity has committed itself to combating the root causes and consequences of modern slavery and human trafficking. Through this partnership with IOM, we are calling on the compassion and generosity of the Muslim community to help free people who are victims of exploitation and restore to them their rights, their dignity and their opportunities for the future."

a1470.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a1470.speech: has publicly stated that he relies on divine intervention to address the country's economic challenges ; has confessed in public forums that he does not know much about certain critical issues.

a1470.speaker: Catholic Bishops' Pastoral Letter
a1470.speech: echoes this sentiment, urging citizens to choose leaders who prioritize the nation's well-being over personal interests.

a1470.speaker: Hon. Allan Ngumuya
a1470.speech: emphasized that Malawians need a leader who can bring fresh ideas and energy to the table while remaining committed to the nation's progress.

a1548.speaker: Alessandra Saibene, coordinator of MSF's emergency response
a1548.speech: "Given the scale of the emergency, and with so many people displaced from their homes in such a short space of time, getting shelter, essential relief items, water, hygiene and health services in place is a priority" ; "Most people left their homes in a hurry and arrived with nothing. Families are sleeping on the floor in vacant buildings, like schools or churches, and sometimes even on the bare ground outside with only banana leaves or a plastic sheet for cover." ; "When so many people live together in crowded and cramped conditions, with limited access to clean water and insufficient latrines, the risk of outbreaks of communicable diseases is very high. We need to act quickly to improve the conditions in the sites where displaced people are staying, otherwise the situation will only get worse."

a1548.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a1548.speech: After an initial assessment of the crisis, has launched an emergency response to address the most urgent needs of displaced people, and, in coordination with other humanitarian actors, is urgently building latrines and installing water and sanitation infrastructure in Kochere and Gedeb districts, trucking in clean water and improving hygiene and water access in local health facilities.

a1567.speaker: António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1567.speech: Says there is a greater effort required for a just energy transition; also calls on leaders to do more to grow economies post the Covid-19 pandemic. Says he told the BRICS leaders that more needs to be done to address the world's problems; speaks of the Russian invasion of Ukraine and says he fears a fractured globe.

a1567.speaker: António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1567.speech: Says the world has changed, and so the global institutions should also change. "This is why we want reforms that are more responsive to the developing countries. Two areas require reform: The UN Security Council and the Bretton Woods Institutions. If we don't we will get to fracturedness. We need to act in solidarity," he says.

a1567.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1567.speech: Announced at a press briefing on Thursday that Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates will join the BRICS bloc from 1 January 2024, after 23 countries expressed interest in joining.

a1567.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1567.speech: Says the BRICS nations are ready to tackle reform in the global finance systems; the issue of local currency payment instruments for intra-trade will be dealt with by the central bank governors of the BRICS nations, and there were deliberations on local currency trade and alternative payment systems. Says there is a need for a fundamental reform of global finance institutions and that the New Development Bank (BRICS Bank) has been a good alternative to other financial institutions. Says BRICS countries received four times greater investment than 20 years ago, but protectionism from some nations is eroding global development. "Facilitating trade and investments is crucial," he says.

a1567.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1567.speech: Opens proceedings welcoming all BRICS heads of state: "Over the past decade BRICS has been a major driver of global growth, trade and investment as well BRICS stands for inclusivity and a more equitable order. It also stands for sustainable development." Says advancing the Africa agenda is imperative for SA's chairpersonship of BRICS: "We are pleased that all BRICS members are re-engaging the African continent in a meaningful way. Russia has always had good relations with Africa. China has assisted Africa with its development goals. India continues its trade with Africa. We are deeply engaged with Africa." Says BRICS nations should advance the growth of countries in the global south, that commitments made by bigger countries should be followed through, and raises concerns that financial systems are being used in wars between nations.

a1567.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1567.speech: At the BRICS business forum, says business leaders see immense opportunities in South Africa and Africa; says BRICS is growing in its importance and influence in the world — "We will be taking into account the various desires of many countries wanting to be part of BRICS"; says South Africa has a strong financial system and deep capital markets — "We have skills and an abundance of natural resources"; reiterates that there should be a greater investment in women-owned businesses, saying many women have been held back due to apartheid and colonialism; says the minerals and commodities Africa has should be refined and processed locally and the continent should export completed goods, not just minerals and materials; and asks business leaders to join their respective governments to address the most pressing social issues.

a1567.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1567.speech: At the China state visit, thanked China for its support in helping South Africa emerge from its crippling loadshedding crisis: "This includes the donation of emergency power equipment worth R167 million and availing a grant of approximately R500 million as development assistance." Says South Africa maintains high-level cooperation with China in trade, politics and most recently energy; says the MoUs signed are a testament to the deep relations between the two countries; says they have agreed to consult on issues of common concern such as BRICS and discussed the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, adding that South Africa is encouraged that Xi welcomed the Africa peace mission to both countries. "With those words President Xi we welcome you with warm arms and in us you have a true friend and we know that in you we also have a true friend."

a1567.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a1567.speech: Says there were in-depth discussions on global issues and consensus was reached; says leaders were unanimous to include the six countries as new members of BRICS and that the membership expansion is historic. Says the expansion of BRICS is a new starting point for BRICS cooperation and to further the cause for world peace and development: "The future will be bright for BRICS countries."

a1567.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a1567.speech: Says the BRICS summit comes at a time when the world is going through turbulence and change: "We need to bring to the world more certainty, and a bigger positive energy. Challenges in developing countries are even more difficult. We should focus on practical cooperation and bolster economic trade and financial exchanges." Says countries ganging up and creating their own laws should be avoided: "BRICS countries should work towards multilateralism and not create small groupings and blocs. We need to bring more countries into the BRICS-family. We need to pull our strength for a just society." He also adds his voice to talks around regulating Artificial Intelligence, saying there should be a BRICS working group on the matter.

a1567.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a1567.speech: At the China state visit says it is his fourth state visit to South Africa and that he feels a "particular warmth" to South Africa, saying that under Ramaphosa's leadership South Africa is a serious player in the world; says this year marks 25 years of relations between the two countries; says the two countries need to continue to support each other on issues where they share common interests, that China is prepared to import more quality products from South Africa and encourage Chinese businesses to do business with South Africa; says China agreed to step up cooperation in education and tourism; says China supports South Africa in playing a strategic role on international stages; says the key to the two countries' strong bond in friendship is that they are connected by a deep bond as comrades and brothers, and that he is ready to make joint efforts with Ramaphosa to take their partnerships to great heights.

a1567.speaker: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India
a1567.speech: Says under SA's presidency in BRICS, countries in the global south have been given priority: "We are making efforts to move forward together with all countries. India supports the expansion of BRICS membership and we welcome moving forward on this using consensus. BRICS will be breaking barrier and revitalising economies." Says he is pleased that the teams agreed on the guiding principles, standards and criteria for the expansion of BRICS and that based on this the six countries have been included in the bloc; congratulates the leaders of those countries; says the expansion and modernisation of BRICS is a message that all global organisations have to adapt to global times; says he is confident there will be new momentum in the bloc, and commends Ramaphosa for the successful organisation of the summit.

a1567.speaker: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India
a1567.speech: Says BRICS has risen as a ray of hope for the global economy: "The last two decades have been a long journey for BRICS. Our New Development Bank is playing a major role. We have created a financial safety net. We are bringing about changes in the lives of ordinary people in BRICS countries." ; "Despite volatility in the world economy, India is the fastest growing economy. India has converted crises and difficulties into opportunities." ; "The number of airports have doubled over the past nine years. India is among the world's leaders in the area of renewable energy. It is but natural that India will become a huge market for renewable energy."

a1567.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a1567.speech: Delivering a closing statement via video link, lauded Ramaphosa's diplomatic skills in handling the negotiations including the issue around the expansion, and congratulated the new BRICS members who will assume full membership next year; says they will establish relevant rules and procedures now that there are new members, and that BRICS' importance and relevance will grow in the world.

a1567.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a1567.speech: Says the group of five countries is a major player in the global arena and its significance is growing — "We deal with the most pressing issues of the world"; speaks of the sanctions imposed on his country, calling them illegal and damaging to the world economy at large — "It is the most vulnerable poor countries that are being hit the hardest"; says BRICS nations have surpassed the G7 countries in terms of economic activity — "This summit is to discuss the detailed transition to national currencies for trade between our countries. The BRICS Bank has a great role to play in this effort"; says a BRICS permanent council on transport is needed — "Should partners agree on that, we will use our chairpersonship to advocate for this"; and announces that Russia will chair BRICS next year with more than 200 public and political events, with the 2024 summit to be held in October in Kazan.

a1567.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a1567.speech: Says Russia stands for greater cooperation to expand energy and agricultural products: "We make a significant contribution to food security for countries in need. These issues were discussed in-depth at the recent Russia-Africa Summit." Says Russia has the capacity to replace Ukraine as a supplier of grain to poor countries and has already agreed to provide six countries with grain, including free delivery. Reiterates that BRICS makes a significant contribution to a healthy global economy and the development targets of the United Nations: "I am confident that BRICS Business Council will continue their creative work."

a1567.speaker: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a1567.speech: In his opening address says Johannesburg was an integral part of the fight against apartheid and that the BRICS formation now faces greater challenges: "We know where the current path of the world can take us. It is unacceptable for the world. We are all suffering the consequences of the war. The Ukraine war shows the limitations of the UN." Says the Ukraine war shows the limitations of the UN Security Council, that BRICS is a forum to discuss peace and safety, and that Brazil is ready to join efforts to effect and contribute towards an immediate ceasefire. He also touched on climate change, saying it is very difficult to fight climate change while many developing countries have to deal with hunger, poverty and violence.

a1567.speaker: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a1567.speech: Says an international financial system is needed that will help emerging countries, and that developing countries cannot be charged high interest rates while richer countries get lower rates: "We can offer our own financial systems to countries in the global south to reduce vulnerabilities." Says BRICS member states have surpassed the G7 countries in terms of economic growth; says BRICS provides a better solution to global financial systems and reiterates that it cannot accept the "colonial systems"; says they hope to mobilise billions to improve infrastructure and green hydrogen technology — "In order for investment to grow, we need to ensure more predictability and political certainties for the business community."

a1567.speaker: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a1567.speech: Says trade between Africa and Brazil dropped significantly since 2013 and that the trade partnership is still in its infancy — "There is plenty of room to grow"; says Brazilian agricultural techniques can be emulated across the African continent and that pocket farming should be implemented to prevent families from starving and ensure food security.

a1567.speaker: Naledi Pandor, South African International Relations Minister
a1567.speech: Says it is becoming clear that everyone wants to be a part of BRICS: “BRICS has become a concept that has taken root in the popular discourse. You are seeing the growth in interest from different sectors. The governments are keen to see greater collaboration. What is absolutely great is the momentum is coming from stakeholders. Given the size we are talking of thousands coming together.” Pandor spoke during a radio interview on the sidelines of the summit.

a1567.speaker: Clayson Monyela, Department of International Relations and Cooperation
a1567.speech: Told journalists that Ramaphosa's delayed press briefing should start at around 9:30.

a1567.speaker: Sim Tshabalala, Standard Bank Group CEO
a1567.speech: Presenting the business forum's outcomes, says South Africa faces serious challenges — "But we have immense strengths and opportunities. We have a free-flowing currency and deep and liquid capital markets"; says China is Africa's biggest trading partner and other BRICS member states also want to invest and trade with the continent, citing IMF estimates that growth in Africa will boom by 2030; says across the BRICS nations there is a greater need for intra-trade between member states especially in agriculture; and says that from an African point of view there were discussions of the pan-African payment system to reduce cross-border costs — "It's important to be realistic of a reserve currency. One of the issues to consider is the large availability of such a currency."

a1567.speaker: Patrice Motsepe, billionaire and inaugural chairperson of the SA Chapter of the BRICS Business Council
a1567.speech: Says South Africa has to position itself as a nation that produces goods and place a greater focus on the African economy and its markets — "As Africa, we have to focus on the positive"; says South African companies are the largest traders on the continent and there is a need for better visa regimes on the continent, especially for businesses — "The BRICS Business Council is a great tool to drive consistent engagements between business and the government. Hurdles and impediments can be removed"; says there is a need for urgency from businesses and government to implement the big plans of the continent to allow for expansion and growth; and, in a post quoted on the BRICSza account, “We don't have time for talk-shops. We have a history with #BRICS as Africa given our history. We want to use that history to build very strong, mutually beneficial business and investment ties. This partnership must result in quantifiable investments”.

a1567.speaker: Ebrahim Patel, South African Trade and Industry Minister
a1567.speech: Delivers a monologue in his opening speech, making it clear that his job was simple, "to open proceedings"; later announces the end of Day 1 proceedings.

a1567.speaker: Asanda Luwaca, National Youth Development Agency chairperson
a1567.speech: Delivers an address to the plenary: "We believe that BRICS countries in general should use their collective strength to guide their work in areas of trade, education, health and wellbeing and social cohesion."

a1567.speaker: Wang Wentao, Chinese Minister of Commerce (speaking on behalf of President Xi Jinping)
a1567.speech: Says the world does not want another cold war: "It wants a clean and peaceful world. Many emerging markets have become strong after shaking off the yoke of colonialism." Says China remains committed to a shared future with countries in the global south: "Hegemony is not in China's DNA. We stand firmly on the right side of history."

a1567.speaker: Wamkele Mene, Secretary-General of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
a1567.speech: Addressing the BRICS Business Forum, says the AfCFTA is very ambitious and it's the first time this continental trade agreement is discussed in a BRICS forum.

a1567.speaker: Gwede Mantashe, ANC national chairperson
a1567.speech: Says people should rely less on the government to take them out of poverty, telling South Africans to take themselves out of poverty.

a1567.speaker: Fikile Mbalula, ANC secretary-general
a1567.speech: Said after the bilateral meeting with Brazil's President Lula da Silva that there had been discussions about surviving political difficulties and facing coalition governance.

a1567.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) statement
a1567.speech: In a statement, the ANC said: "The meeting will focus on existing political ties between the ANC and Brazil's governing Workers Party, as well as other issues of mutual interest."

a1567.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, South African Finance Minister
a1567.speech: Told News24 that China donated gifts of emergency electricity equipment worth R167 million and opened its market for South Africa's avocados, but that trading between the two countries in US dollars is here to stay.

a1567.speaker: The Presidency of South Africa
a1567.speech: Said this week it hoped the agreements with China would focus "on socio-economic cooperation which both sides will ensure implementation that yield results for both our peoples"; said it expected to cultivate a "win-win partnership" with China and wanted to "underscore the urgent need to address trade balance and diversify South African exports to China by identifying broad market access for value-added products".

a1567.speaker: Stella Ndabeni-Abrahams, Small Business Development Minister
a1567.speech: Is in support of a BRICS visa for entrepreneurs to grow economic trade among the bloc member states, after billionaire Patrice Motsepe called for special BRICS visas for entrepreneurs.

a1567.speaker: Sbu Zondi, Build One South Africa (BOSA) spokesperson
a1567.speech: Says SA's hosting of the 15th BRICS summit is a significant event for the country at a time when the "Madiba-glow of global reputation" has lost its lustre in some quarters, and the currency has plummeted. "South Africa's foreign policy of late lurches from ill-founded statement to crisis management. In the modern era, a country's economic fortunes, the global application of its cultural values and the aspirations of its citizens must be aligned. With the notable exception of our participation in both BRICS and in the AU, South Africa has not guided her international relations agenda based on our country's national interests."

a1567.speaker: Ukrainian Association of South Africa and Amnesty International South Africa (protesters)
a1567.speech: Protested at Innesfree Park in Sandton calling for the world to stand with Ukraine; they urged the world's nations to stand against the Russian aggression and called on President Cyril Ramaphosa to condemn Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the ill-treatment of Ukrainian children.

a1567.speaker: Amhara movement group (Ethiopian protesters)
a1567.speech: A group of not more than 30 Ethiopians say they are the Amhara movement group requesting the BRICS leaders not to accept the Ethiopian government's request to be part of BRICS.

a1567.speaker: Bheki Cele, South African Police Minister
a1567.speech: Defended the considerable deployment of police officers in Sandton for the summit.

a1567.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a1567.speech: Say the debate on a new financial order and a common BRICS currency is going nowhere, and that the creation of a common currency and a new financial world order — as envisaged by China — is still a pipe dream.

a1567.speaker: Patrick Bond, analyst
a1567.speech: Examines at least five areas where things went wrong for the BRICS bloc, arguing that before the 2023 summit in South Africa BRICS came close to toppling.

a1567.speaker: Chinese and Indian officials (anonymous)
a1567.speech: News24 understands officials from China and India had flagged concerns about protest action against Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

a1626.speaker: Government of Zanzibar (Revolutionary Government, SMZ)
a1626.speech: While increasing the area under irrigated agriculture from 875 hectares in 2019 to 2,300 hectares in 2024, it has urged citizens to abandon habitual/traditional farming in order to achieve the goals of self-sufficiency in food and in commerce.

a1626.speaker: Shamata Shaame Khamis, Zanzibar Minister of Agriculture, Irrigation, Natural Resources and Livestock
a1626.speech: Speaking at the launch of irrigation infrastructure improvements on December 8, 2024 in four upgraded valleys, said the Government's intention is to uplift its farmers, increase food production and grow national income: "There are organisations that came wanting to take these valleys, but the Government said it is giving them to its own citizens, so it has improved the infrastructure so that there can be sufficient production for two seasons" ; "Anyone who sees that his capacity is small will not be able to farm for two seasons - let him step aside, because we would not at all want these opportunities and these efforts to be toyed with; a lot of money has been spent and we have good intentions, so let us unite to produce so we can encourage our leaders for our development." According to Shamata, they want the valleys used for two seasons with two different crops: "when they finish growing rice they should move into vegetable farming, which also has great demand in Zanzibar."

a1626.speaker: Khamis Ali, Permanent Secretary of the Zanzibar Ministry of Agriculture
a1626.speech: Said that for farmers who have begun using the infrastructure, production has increased from 1.5 tonnes to 5.5 tonnes in a single season: "So in two seasons a farmer produces 11 tonnes, and this is the Government's plan to move away from habitual farming."

a1626.speaker: Eunju Ahn, Ambassador of South Korea to Tanzania
a1626.speech: Said the project began in 2019 and that they will continue to cooperate with Zanzibar to ensure the project is sustainable and brings benefit to the nation and its citizens.

a1626.speaker: Michael Battle, Ambassador of the United States to Tanzania
a1626.speech: Said that together they have expanded the programme to bring year-round benefits to members of that community: "This improved irrigation scheme now fully covers Unguja and Pemba; this international cooperation has enabled thousands of Tanzanians to increase productivity in agriculture and to raise domestic income substantially." He said they are proud to increase the impact of the irrigation programme and turn it into a year-round operation, improving the quality of rice harvests in the main farming season, expanding horticulture opportunities in the off-season, and increasing use of the irrigation system throughout the year.

a1626.speaker: Pili Kashinje, vegetable and fruit farmer
a1626.speech: Said that when she started moving into farming it seemed like a big job, but after getting used to it she is proud to have started getting markets inside and outside the country: "At first it was a challenge because it seemed I could not do it, but I gained confidence in farming and now I supply vegetables and fruit to hotels."

a1626.speaker: Ussi Makame, farmer
a1626.speech: "Right now I am engaged in this farming, so people should be motivated to farm because it is good work and it pays if a person follows all the instructions and guidelines."

a1684.speaker: Annette Ssemuwemba, EAC Deputy Secretary General in charge of Customs, Trade and Monetary Affairs
a1684.speech: Welcomed all participants to the trade fair: "We are excited to welcome participants from across the region to Juba for this dynamic event. The trade fair represents a vital opportunity for entrepreneurs to showcase their contributions to the economy, share experiences, and build lasting connections that will help drive our regional growth." ; The Deputy Secretary General said that the fair is expected to attract thousands of visitors, including business owners, practitioners, policymakers and members of the general public, all eager to explore the unique offerings and innovations presented by the MSMEs of East Africa.

a1713.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1713.speech: Said that since 26 January, nearly 3,000 people have been killed and 2,880 injured in attacks by the M23 and their allies "with heavy weapons used in populated areas, and intense fighting against the armed forces of the DRC and their allies." ; Addressing the emergency session, he noted that two hospitals in Goma had been bombed on 27 January, killing and injuring multiple patients, including women and children, and that in a mass prison break at Muzenze Prison in Goma on the same day, at least 165 female inmates were reportedly raped and most were later killed in a fire under suspicious circumstances, citing the authorities.

a1713.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1713.speech: "I am horrified by the spread of sexual violence, which has been an appalling feature of this conflict for a long time. This is likely to worsen in the current circumstances," adding that UN staff were now verifying multiple allegations of rape, gang rape and sexual slavery in eastern DRC's conflict zones.

a1713.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1713.speech: Called for greater understanding of the political and economic background of the conflict: "The population in the eastern DRC is suffering terribly, while many of the products we consume or use, such as mobile phones, are created using minerals from the east of the country. We are all implicated."

a1713.speaker: Draft resolution circulated before the Human Rights Council Special Session
a1713.speech: Condemned Rwanda's military support of the M23 armed group and called for both Rwanda and M23 to halt their advance and to allow lifesaving humanitarian access immediately.

a1713.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the Secretary-General in the DRC and head of the UN peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO)
a1713.speech: Told the Council that dead bodies still lie in the streets of Goma, which M23 fighters now control, and that the situation is "catastrophic." "While I am speaking, youth are being subjected to forced recruitments and human rights defenders, civil society actors and journalists have also become a major population at risk. MONUSCO continues to receive requests for individual protection from them as well as from judicial authorities under threat and at risk of reprisals from M23 in areas under its control." ; She issued a stark warning on the health risks linked to ongoing fighting, "especially the resurgence of cholera and the high risk of mpox, the sudden interruption of children's schooling, and the rise of conflict-related sexual violence and gender-based violence"; she said that according to latest reports, medical personnel face electricity cuts and lack fuel for their generators for basic services, including morgues, and added: "I again call on international community to advocate for humanitarian assistance to reach Goma immediately."

a1713.speaker: Patrick Muyaya Katembwe, DRC Minister of Communications and Media
a1713.speech: Spoke out against the continued logistical, military and financial support of countries including Rwanda "to armed groups operating on our territory." The minister maintained that Rwanda's support for the M23 had fuelled the violence in eastern DRC "for more than 30 years, exacerbating the war for reasons linked to the exploitation of the strategic mining resources of the Democratic Republic of Congo."

a1713.speaker: Ambassador James Ngango, Rwanda's Ambassador to the UN in Geneva
a1713.speech: Dismissing the DRC claim, insisted that a large-scale attack against Rwanda was "imminent." He accused the "Kinshasa-backed coalition" of stockpiling a large number of weapons and military equipment near Rwanda's border, mostly in or around Goma airport. "These weapons include rockets, kamikaze drones, heavy artillery guns capable of shooting precisely within the Rwandan territory. The weapons were not turned at the theatre of operations against the M23, rather they were pointed directly at Rwanda."

a1713.speaker: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) / Human Rights Council resolution
a1713.speech: The Human Rights Council's 47 Members adopted a resolution establishing a fact-finding mission into abuses, staffed by OHCHR, to start work as quickly as possible; OHCHR said at the outcome of the Special Session that a commission of inquiry will take over the fact-finding mission's work once its commissioners are appointed.

a1729.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a1729.speech: On peace and reconciliation: "We cannot bring the gospel of hatred and violence, we must have a message of love for our neighbour. That is why all religions teach love. Let us work close to the people for the consolidation of peace and reconciliation. Let us do everything to stabilise the country and put an end to violent demonstrations." ; "Politicians must preach love, forgiveness and reconciliation among Mozambicans; only then will we manage to have peace." ; "Thinking differently is good, but that fact cannot lead us to violence, which generates violence, hatred which generates hatred. The law of life says that each one reaps what he sows; all Mozambicans must plant love starting at home."

a1729.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a1729.speech: On the recently signed political commitment: "The signing of the political commitment is not the end; on the contrary it is the beginning, and everyone must take part. The media, businesspeople, academia, all of us have to sit down to debate what is happening to us, because over these thirty years, whenever elections are held there are problems afterwards. Let us debate the deep causes of this problem."

a1729.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a1729.speech: On dependence on external aid: expressed the conviction that independence will be complete when Mozambique no longer needs external aid for its general budget: "Independence will be complete when we do not need to depend on others; that is why we say, let us work, produce in industry and even for export."

a1729.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a1729.speech: On the 50th anniversary of independence: evoked the 50 years of independence being completed this year, stressing that "the 50th anniversary celebration should be held in an atmosphere of peace and harmony and never divided; let us spend the celebration as brothers."

a1839.speaker: 2023 Human Rights Practices Report, compiled by the United States Department of State Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labour
a1839.speech: Shows that Zambia did not record any reports of political prisoners or detainees; under the Political Prisoners and Detainees section, the report indicates that "there were no reports of political prisoners or detainees"; notes that Government did not restrict or disrupt access to the internet.

a1965.speaker: United States government
a1965.speech: Has expressed its willingness to continue supporting humanitarian projects under way in Mozambique, including the assistance aimed at fighting against HIV/AIDS.

a1965.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a1965.speech: Speaking to reporters on Wednesday in Maputo after being granted an audience by Mozambican President Daniel Chapo, said the US is open to continue working with Mozambique, despite the challenges that the country has been facing; pledged that support from the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) will continue ; “We have exemptions on some projects that save lives, that is, PEPFAR projects, the supply of antiretroviral drugs, but also logistics for the health sector and we are going to continue our programmes to save the lives of the two million Mozambicans who have HIV” ; according to Vrooman, the US government has humanitarian assistance programmes in Mozambique, so “these will continue as well, and we work with partners here, with the Mozambican government, the private sector and also NGOs to safeguard the humanitarian assistance programmes.”

a2045.speaker: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a2045.speech: Under the Rome Statute, "intentional attacks against personnel, installations, material, units or vehicles involved in a humanitarian assistance or peacekeeping mission in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations" that are entitled to civilian protections are war crimes in both international and non-international armed conflicts ; Article 87(7) provides: "Where a state party fails to comply with a request to cooperate by the court contrary to the provisions of the statute, thereby preventing the court from exercising its functions and power under the statute, the court may make a finding to that effect and refer the matter to the assembly of state parties or, where the Security Council referred the matter to the court, to the Security Council."

a2045.speaker: Law of treaties
a2045.speech: The law of treaties obliges these states to refrain from "acts which would defeat the object and purpose of the treaty until they declare they do not intend to become a party to the treaty."

a2045.speaker: Satellite imagery analysis (5 October 2024)
a2045.speech: On 5 October 2024, satellite imagery analysis found that new Israeli military activity was visible near UNIFIL position 6-52 where at least 30 military vehicles of the Israeli Defence Force (IDF) were present near the UNIFIL position.

a2045.speaker: United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)
a2045.speech: On 6 October, UNIFIL publicly raised concerns regarding Israel's military activities immediately adjacent to its mission's position southeast of Maroun el-Ras in Lebanon.

a2045.speaker: Israeli military
a2045.speech: Made a request to UNIFIL to relocate more than five kilometres from the Israel-Lebanon border "as soon as possible, in order to maintain their safety".

a2045.speaker: UN peacekeeping chief
a2045.speech: Totally refused the Israeli military request that UNIFIL relocate more than five kilometres from the Israel-Lebanon border.

a2045.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
a2045.speech: As of 11 October 2024, the CPJ preliminary investigation showed that at least 128 journalists and media workers were killed in the West Bank, Gaza, Israel and Lebanon since the war began.

a2045.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a2045.speech: On 19 July 2024, the ICJ found that: "It is plausible that Israel's actions amount to genocide, and Israel's occupation and annexation of Palestinian territories are unlawful, and its discriminatory laws and policies against Palestinians violate the prohibition and racial segregation and apartheid."

a2072.speaker: USAID
a2072.speech: According to USAID, since 1990, South Africa's national average temperature has increased twice as fast as global temperatures.

a2072.speaker: The Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America
a2072.speech: Sees a clear link between warmer temperatures and longer pollen seasons, reporting that warmer weather has caused the pollen season to be 11 to 27 days longer.

a2072.speaker: US Department of Agriculture (research)
a2072.speech: Shows that pollen seasons now feature 21% more pollen than in 1990.

a2072.speaker: The School of Public Health (SPH) at Harvard University
a2072.speech: Says that, in addition to warmer conditions causing plants to bloom earlier and for longer, the greenhouse emissions that are the main cause of climate change are causing higher levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and this is stimulating plants to produce and release more pollen.

a2072.speaker: Solenco (importer of dehumidifiers)
a2072.speech: Offers three top tips for preventing hay fever: always shower before bed, because pollen and other allergens get trapped in hair during the day and make their way into airways; don't remove your nose hair, because the hairs act as a defensive wall that keeps allergens out; and allergy-proof your home by keeping doors and windows closed in the early morning and evening, favouring tiled floors over carpets and dusting with a damp cloth.

a2072.speaker: Trevor Brewer, Solenco air treatment specialist
a2072.speech: Says too much moisture in the air can encourage mould, which can also bring about allergies, and recommends that people who live in damp or humid regions invest in a dehumidifier to prevent damp and mould from forming in their homes.

a2072.speaker: Claire Bowen, brand manager for Shower to Shower
a2072.speech: "As we transition from winter to spring, [you should] use this time to transition into new habits, routines, and activities. Get ready to jump - or spring - into something new!" ; "Shed the weight of disorganisation by decluttering your living space. Start small and move room by room, sorting items into categories like 'keep', 'donate', or 'discard'. A decluttered environment makes room for new experiences and ideas to blossom." ; "With the weather warming up and nature coming alive, take advantage of the outdoors by trading indoor workouts for outdoor activities like jogging, hiking, or biking. Get some fresh air and enjoy the added endorphins!"

a2171.speaker: Communique of the Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Living Abroad
a2171.speech: "The Kingdom of Morocco, whose Sovereign, His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist him, chairs the Al-Quds Committee, welcomes the progress made towards halting the hostilities and attacks against civilians that began on 7 October 2023. The Kingdom calls on all Palestinian and Israeli parties to give peace a chance and to demonstrate sincere and constructive commitment, far from any circumstantial or opportunistic considerations" ; the Kingdom expresses the wish that this ceasefire agreement be fully respected, and that it allow the halt of attacks against civilians, the return of displaced persons and the smooth access of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities ; the ceasefire agreement should open the way to a real peace process, allowing the establishment of a Palestinian State within the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side and in peace with Israel.

a2171.speaker: His Majesty King Mohammed VI, King of Morocco and President of the Al-Quds Committee
a2171.speech: As he stressed, notably in His Royal Message to the last Arab Summit, it is essential to avoid coming out of one crisis only to enter another.

a2505.speaker: United States Embassy in Djibouti
a2505.speech: Announced on January 5, 2022 a new donation by the American government of 29,250 doses of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine as part of the US administration's global efforts to fight the COVID-19 pandemic, stating that the donation, coordinated by COVAX, will help protect the population of Djibouti, particularly people under 18, and prevent the spread of new strains of the virus, and that the American government fully supports the vaccination efforts of the Djiboutian authorities and encourages everyone to get vaccinated.

a2505.speaker: Andrea Tomaszewicz, Deputy Chief of Mission of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a2505.speech: Underlined the long-standing commitment of the United States to ensuring access to health services for the population of Djibouti, and the necessity of this assistance, which is even more important today as everyone faces together the challenges of the new COVID-19 variants.

a2556.speaker: Orbitly INC (with its subsidiary eHealth IT Services PLC / Orbit Health) (announcement)
a2556.speech: Announced that it has successfully closed its first external seed-investment, co-led by Africa-based Savannah VC fund and New York-based Betam Group, LLC, along with other diaspora HNW investors.

a2556.speaker: Pazion Chernet, Co-Founder & CEO of Orbitly
a2556.speech: “It gives me great pleasure to welcome our strategic investors that will position us from a startup to high rise, with their tremendous VC funding and growth experience and wisdom. I am especially proud to announce our first external fund raise that coincided with our double win in digitizing Ethiopia's healthcare with our partners JSI, USAID and Ethiopia's Ministry of Health. We started Orbitly with a firm belief that a healthy society is the foundation of a productive society and we will do our part in changing the misconceptions that living a healthy life in Sub-Saharan Africa is a luxury, by helping strengthen the weak healthcare infrastructure, through end-to-end innovative technology solutions. This fund raise will enable us to deliver on our promise, at scale and we are extremely hopeful of what the future holds for us and our clients.”

a2584.speaker: Namibian Electoral Commission
a2584.speech: announced on 3 December 2024 the election of Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah (NNN) to the head of Namibia, reportedly winning the presidential election in the first round with 57.31% against Panduleni Itula of the Independent Patriots for Change (IPC), who came second with 25.50%.

a2584.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, Vice-President and president-elect of Namibia
a2584.speech: throughout the campaign put forward her age and her experience as guarantees of wisdom and stability, and promised her people the stability of the country; her social project was built around the creation of jobs in a country heavily hit by unemployment, thanks to attracting foreign investors who could exploit its main mineral wealth, uranium.

a2584.speaker: World Bank
a2584.speech: according to which Namibia is the second most unequal country on the planet.

a2606.speaker: Hamas (statement)
a2606.speech: “Yesterday [Thursday], the Hamas delegation received a proposal from the mediators to resume negotiations. Responsibly, the movement responded positively and presented its answer this morning, including its agreement to release the Israeli soldier Idan Alexander, who holds US citizenship, as well as [to return] the bodies of four other [hostages] with dual nationality.”

a2606.speaker: Hamas (statement)
a2606.speech: Reiterated its “total readiness” to reach a comprehensive agreement including everything agreed for the second phase and again called on Israel to “fully comply with its obligations”; did not reveal the date on which it intends to release a new hostage or hand over the remains.

a2606.speaker: Israeli press
a2606.speech: Reported on Thursday that the new proposal, backed by US special envoy Steve Witkoff, called for the release of five living hostages in exchange for a 50-day ceasefire in Gaza, during which negotiations would be held on the continuation of the agreement.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: Says AHF is celebrating a significant milestone – over 2 million lives are now receiving HIV care globally under its watch; says that as the largest provider of HIV/AIDS medical care worldwide, AHF’s commitment to providing pioneering treatment and advocacy regardless of the ability to pay has never been more evident, and that this achievement highlights its relentless pursuit of a world free from AIDS and the significant strides made, particularly in Nigeria.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: States that AHF’s mission is rooted in the principle of delivering high-quality medical care and advocacy to all individuals regardless of their financial status, supported by an extensive network of pharmacies, thrift stores, healthcare contracts and strategic partnerships, and that its approach combines innovative treatment methods, comprehensive care and robust advocacy.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: Says AHF officially commenced HIV/AIDS service provision in Nigeria in August 2011 in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH-NASCP), SMOH and NACA; that as of August 2024 AHF Nigeria supports 28,480 People Living with HIV/AIDS with free comprehensive anti-retroviral therapy, antibiotics, drugs for non-communicable diseases and free laboratory services across seven states; that it has conducted over 2.4 million HIV tests, distributed more than 26 million free condoms and awarded over USD 375,000 in grants to community-based and civil society organisations; and that it has supported the training of over 2,000 government healthcare workers.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: Says AHF partnered mainly with the Federal Government of Nigeria through the Ministry of Health, NACA and the State Ministries of Health, while actively collaborating with international funding bodies like PEPFAR and its partners, including the Global Fund, with AHF donating $10 million to the Fund during the last replenishment effort; says these partnerships have been instrumental in scaling up services and improving treatment outcomes.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: Says that despite its achievements AHF still faces challenges general to the national HIV/AIDS landscape — stigma continues to hinder access to care, especially in conservative areas, and reaching individuals in remote regions and addressing new infections require innovation, resources and detailed consistency.

a2633.speaker: Ijezie, Country Program Director, AHF Nigeria (AIDS Healthcare Foundation)
a2633.speech: Says AHF Nigeria is committed to broadening its reach by enhancing free service delivery, strengthening outreach, increasing awareness, combating stigma and providing education on HIV prevention and treatment; says the fight against HIV/AIDS requires continued support, advocacy and innovation and that AHF is fully committed, “with our edge of being a program and not a project – which means our commitment is not time bound. We are motivated to do more until we win the fight against AIDS.”

a2706.speaker: Monroe Doctrine (adopted 1823 by the United States)
a2706.speech: Asserted that European powers would not be allowed to interfere in the Western Hemisphere, effectively establishing Latin America as a U.S. sphere of influence.

a2706.speaker: Woodrow Wilson, U.S. President
a2706.speech: Pointed out that colonialism amounted to an oppressive boot on the neck of nations' self-determination.

a2706.speaker: 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act (document)
a2706.speech: Explicitly committed its signatories to avoid establishing spheres of influence, directing NATO and Russia to aim to create "in Europe a common space of security and stability, without dividing lines or spheres of influence limiting the sovereignty of any state."

a2706.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President (recent speeches)
a2706.speech: It is clear from his many recent speeches that he had never really abandoned an understanding of geopolitics that rested on spheres of influence and always struggled to understand why NATO should continue to exist, much less to expand.

a2706.speaker: Russia and Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a2706.speech: Have demanded that Ukraine accept territorial losses and remain outside Western military alliances, an outcome that would render the country a satellite of Russia.

a2816.speaker: Russell Vought, director of the Office of Management and Budget
a2816.speech: Told reporters after lunch with Republican senators that Trump could accept a change in the measure to exempt PEPFAR: “There is a substitute amendment that does not include the PEPFAR rescission and we're fine with that.”

a2816.speaker: Lisa Murkowski, US Senator (Republican, Alaska)
a2816.speech: “You don't need to gut the entire Corporation for Public Broadcasting,” said in a Senate speech ; she said the Trump administration also had not provided assurances that battles against diseases such as malaria and polio worldwide would be maintained, along with programs including family planning and pandemic prevention ; but most of all, Murkowski said, Congress must assert its role in deciding how federal funds were spent.

a2816.speaker: John Thune, Senate Majority Leader (Republican, South Dakota)
a2816.speech: Said he expected the House would act quickly to pass the measure.

a2816.speaker: Democratic lawmakers tracking frozen funding
a2816.speech: As of mid-June, Trump was blocking $425 billion in such funds, according to Democratic lawmakers tracking frozen funding.

a2816.speaker: Mike Rounds, US Senator (Republican, South Dakota)
a2816.speech: Was concerned about funding cuts to Native American radio stations, but said on Tuesday he would support the rescissions package after the administration promised to fund some tribal broadcasters separately ; “We're going to have to work our way through that issue,” Rounds said on Tuesday, adding he felt confident Trump's budget office would follow funding guidelines to redirect dollars to tribal media stations.

a2816.speaker: Democrats
a2816.speech: Have said the U.S. withdrawal of “soft power” efforts from the international stage, such as limited emergency assistance after an earthquake in Myanmar, strengthens global adversaries like Russia and China.

a2816.speaker: Charles Schumer, US Senator (New York), Senate Democratic leader
a2816.speech: “It still leaves an enormous vacuum that China and Russia will fill.”

a2816.speaker: Susan Collins, US Senator (Republican, Maine), chair of the Appropriations Committee
