For the poorest countries especially, tax revenue is key to ensure they have the funds needed to fund their development without being reliant on foreign aid.” ; explained that the royalty rate Paladin pays was lowered from the normal 5% of sales to 1.5% for the first three years and then 3%, a tax break “negotiated in secret without public scrutiny” that has cost Malawi US$15.635 million, and that by routing its loan from Malawi to Australia via a Netherlands subsidiary Paladin “lowered its withholding taxes in Malawi by more than US$27.5 million over six years”, lowering its total tax contributions to Malawi by more than US$43 million.

a7075.speaker: ActionAid (recommendations to the Malawi government)
a7075.speech: Recommended ending harmful discretionary tax incentives — ensuring that any tax incentives should be subject to Parliamentary and public scrutiny before being signed and made publicly available immediately upon signature; not reducing royalty rates as a tax incentive to multinational companies; not allowing capitalisation to be thinner than the government's guideline; ensuring future incentives negotiated with international companies, particularly in the extractives sector, are subject to rigorous public cost-benefit studies that are periodically updated and inform tax incentive policy; that government measure and publicly disclose revenue foregone through all tax incentives to multinational companies annually; and that the government consider following Zambia's example and remove stability clauses that are not in Malawi's interests.

a7075.speaker: Investment experts (unnamed)
a7075.speech: Said that at 85% shareholding the Australian company is set to reap astronomical profits, as indicated on various mining internet sites that the spot price of uranium has almost doubled from US$28/lbs in April 2016 to the current US$64/lbs, with demand expected to rise.

a7075.speaker: Greg Bittar, Lotus Resources managing director
a7075.speech: “Formalising this offtake arrangement with a key customer is an important milestone for Lotus as we continue to progress production restart plans at Kayelekera towards our 3rd quarter of 2025 goal.”

a7075.speaker: Mining-technology.com (report)
a7075.speech: Reported that Lotus Resources signed a binding uranium offtake agreement with a North American utility company involving the sale of 600,000lb of triuranium octoxide (U3O8) from the Kayelekera project, scheduled for delivery between 2026 and 2029, and that the contract includes a fixed-price escalation percentage per annum aligned with the Reserve Bank of Australia's long-term inflation target, applicable from the first delivery year, with pricing achieved through competitive discussions ensuring favourable terms for Lotus Resources.

a7452.speaker: Clemence Kato, Senior State Attorney (prosecution)
a7452.speech: Told the Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court that the Republic asks for 21 days to complete the investigation, saying there are a few things they are finalising and therefore asking the court to grant them time so that they can complete that investigation.

a7452.speaker: George Mwalaki, defence lawyer for accused Malekela and Moshi
a7452.speech: Asked the court to set 14 days instead of the 21 days requested by the prosecution side.

a7452.speaker: The accused (jointly)
a7452.speech: Opposed the request because most of them come from outside Dar es Salaam, claiming the transport fare is a problem for them, and asked the court to give guidance on adjourning the case.

a7452.speaker: Simon Aloyce, accused (businessman resident in Mwanza)
a7452.speech: "Your Honour, 14 days will be tight for me because I come from Mwanza; every 14 days I come to court, those days will be somewhat tight for me because of the fare."

a7452.speaker: Julieth Moshi, accused (WP 10050, police officer, resident of Kisarawe)
a7452.speech: "Your Honour, 14 days are tight for many of us because of finding the fare, so we ask that the date of our case be moved forward."

a7452.speaker: Geofrey Mhini, Senior Resident Magistrate
a7452.speech: After hearing the requests of both sides, said that since the accused are out on bail he was adjourning the case until 23 October 2025, when it will be mentioned.

a7452.speaker: Charge sheet, criminal case no. 18451 of 2025 (court record)
a7452.speech: According to the charge sheet, the accused face 16 counts of forging firearm ownership permits, contrary to sections 333, 335A and 337 of the Penal Code, Chapter 16, as revised in 2019; the permits are alleged to have been issued between 5 December 2024 and 4 April 2025, in the names of Ahmed Ally, Ahmed Ahmed Sandrudin, Omary Abdallah, Robert Koka, Fathi Ally, Mohamed Salim, Suleman Mbewa, Mickdad Chakindo, Irfan Nafari, Gulam Abbas Najafi, Ismail Ismail, Salim Salim, Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe and Said Mohamed.
